CatWayOut Privacy Policy

Last updated: November 23, 2026

You play without signing up or logging in, and your game records stay on your device. There are no in-app purchases. The ad service (Unity LevelPlay + Unity Ads) processes device information and advertising identifiers needed to deliver ads; on first launch the game asks whether you allow personalized ads and does not start the ad SDK before you choose. An issue report is sent to TeamCP's report server only when you send one yourself from Settings.

Applies to version 1.0.0. We update this page and its date whenever features or the ad setup change.

1. Scope and operator

TeamCP develops and operates the Android game “CatWayOut” (냥냥 길 비켜, com.teamcp.catwayout). This policy explains what information the game handles and the choices you have. Contact: teamcp.channel@gmail.com.

The game has no sign-up, login, chat or in-app purchases. It does not ask for or collect your name, email, phone number, precise location (GPS), contacts, microphone, camera, photos or storage. The permissions the app itself uses are internet and network state (ads and issue reports), vibration (effects) and the advertising ID (AD_ID). The Android ad services attribution and topics APIs and the WAKE_LOCK, RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED and FOREGROUND_SERVICE permissions come from the ad SDK libraries. If you email support, we use your reply address and message only to answer you.

2. Information stored on your device

This information is kept only in the app's private Android storage to keep your progress and settings. Game records and settings are never sent to a TeamCP server. There is no cloud save, and Android auto backup is turned off for this app, so it is not included in your Google account backup. The app contains no analytics tools (such as Firebase Analytics) and no automatic crash reporting.

  • Game records: best star rating per level, clear count, daily hint use, and a play log of actions and their times
  • Settings: sound effects, vibration, language and your personalized-ads choice
  • Unsent issue reports: a report you sent is kept on the device (up to 50) until the server accepts it, then retried

3. Ads and what the ad services process

The game is free and supported by ads. The ad setup is Unity LevelPlay (ad mediation, Unity Technologies) with Unity Ads. It does not include AdMob, Firebase or any payment SDK.

A TeamCP house banner appears at the bottom of the screen. Once you choose your ad settings and a banner ad is ready, it can take that spot. Tapping the house banner opens the TeamCP website. Interstitial ads may appear between a cleared level and the next one, with limits on frequency and spacing. After your free hints run out, you can choose to watch a rewarded ad to completion for one hint.

To load and show ads, the ad services may process the following information.

  • Advertising and SDK identifiers such as the advertising ID and app set ID
  • Device information such as model, operating system, language, screen, network type and carrier
  • IP address and the approximate region derived from it
  • Interactions such as ad impressions and clicks, and ad-related error and diagnostic information
  • Some information about apps installed on the device (for example, whether an app store is installed)

The purposes are showing and measuring ads, preventing fraud (ad fraud), and, if you agree, personalized ads. The app tells the ad services that it is not directed at children. TeamCP does not receive individual user information collected by the ad services; we only see aggregated revenue and impression statistics in the dashboards.

4. Your ad choices

Your choice is stored only on the device and passed to the ad service (Unity LevelPlay) as a consent signal. Choosing “Only non-personalized ads” also sends a GDPR consent refusal and a do-not-sell (sale/sharing opt-out) signal under certain U.S. state laws.

  • On first launch every user chooses between “Allow personalized ads” and “Only non-personalized ads”. Until you choose, the ad SDK is not started and no ad requests are sent. If you choose non-personalized ads, you see the same number of ads, but they are not personalized.
  • You can choose again at any time in Settings > “Ad consent”.
  • In Android Settings > Privacy > Ads you can reset or delete your advertising ID. When it is deleted, a string of zeros is sent instead and cannot be used for personalized ads.
  • You can ask to access, delete or opt out of ad data through the privacy icon in an ad or the procedure in Unity's policy below.
  • If you turn off the internet connection, no ad requests are made; the game can be played offline.

5. Issue reports

A report is sent only when you write a description in Settings > “Report an issue” and tap send. There are no automatic reports or crash reports. A report contains:

  • The description you write (up to 2,000 characters) and the report type you pick
  • Attached automatically: app name and version, the name of the screen you reported from, app language, device model name, and a random report number created for each report

Reports never include your advertising ID, an account, your game records or your location. Please do not write personal information such as your name or contact details in the description. Reports are sent over an encrypted connection (HTTPS) and stored on a report server operated by TeamCP (web hosting: Cafe24, Republic of Korea), and are used only to find and fix problems. The server and the hosting company may process your IP address in connection logs while the request is handled. Reports stored on the server are kept for 90 days from the day they are received and then deleted; if you ask us to delete one sooner, we delete it right away.

6. Third-party services and international processing

Services from Unity LevelPlay/Unity Technologies and Google (Android ad services) are governed by their own policies. Ad information may be processed outside your country; see each provider's policy for recipients, locations and safeguards. Issue reports are stored on a hosting server in the Republic of Korea.

TeamCP does not sell user information. However, data processing in the ad ecosystem may count as a “sale” or “sharing” under some local laws, so please also review the providers' opt-out and rights information below.

Detailed notice of overseas transfers (added November 23, 2026)

Under Articles 28-8 and 30 of Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA), we list each kind of processing in this game in which personal information is transferred outside Korea. The information below is sent directly from your device to each provider without passing through any server operated by TeamCP. Provider details are based on each provider’s published policy.

Ads — Unity LevelPlay, Unity Ads, ironSource Ads

Recipient and contact
Unity Technologies (Unity Technologies S.F.) — operator of Unity LevelPlay, Unity Ads and ironSource Ads
Contact: DPO@unity3d.com · 116 New Montgomery Street, Suite 200, San Francisco, CA 94105, United States
Destination countries
The United States, plus countries where Unity has facilities (including Israel, where ironSource is headquartered) and countries with data centers of service providers Unity uses (such as Google Cloud Platform) — as stated in Unity’s Game Player and App User Privacy Policy
Data transferred
Advertising identifiers (Google advertising ID, app set ID, etc., to the extent device settings allow), IP address and approximate location derived from it, device model, operating system, app version, language, network information, and ad request, impression, click, completed-view, error and diagnostic information (details in the ads section of this policy)
When and how
Each time the ad SDK initializes or requests, shows or measures an ad while the app is running, sent directly from your device to Unity’s servers over the internet (encrypted connection)
Purpose
Ad mediation and delivery, frequency capping, performance measurement, fraud prevention, error diagnosis
Retention period
Unity states that it keeps data for as long as needed for the processing purposes and may keep it longer when needed for legal obligations or for disputes or investigations (Unity policy section 10, “Retention”). Because Unity does not publish a fixed retention period for general ad data, this policy does not state a separate period.
Legal basis
PIPA Article 28-8(1)(iii)(a) — treated as outsourcing and storage needed to perform the contract for providing a free (ad-supported) game, with the transfer details disclosed in this policy
How to refuse and effect
If you turn off the internet connection, no ad requests or transfers take place. If you delete the advertising ID in Android settings, the advertising ID is not sent. If you do not want any transfer, you can stop using and uninstall the app; in that case you cannot use ads or ad rewards. To access or delete information already transferred, contact Unity (DPO@unity3d.com) or use the privacy icon in the ad.

The following processing takes place in Korea and is not an overseas transfer.

  • Problem reports: reports you send yourself are stored on the report server operated by TeamCP (web hosting: Cafe24, Republic of Korea) and are not transferred abroad.

7. How to delete data, and retention

Game data on the device remains until you delete it. Issue reports sent to the server are deleted 90 days after they are received. Ad information is retained according to each provider's policy. Support emails are not kept longer than needed after we have answered.

  • On the device: uninstall the app, or use Android Settings > Apps > CatWayOut > Storage > Clear data to delete all game data, including settings and unsent reports. Game records are not kept on any TeamCP server.
  • Reports you sent: email teamcp.channel@gmail.com with the date you sent it and your device model (and, if possible, part of the text), and we will find and delete it.
  • Ad information: delete or reset your advertising ID and use the request procedure in Unity's policy. Uninstalling the app alone does not delete information already processed by ad providers.
  • Help: email teamcp.channel@gmail.com with the app name and your request. Do not send passwords or ID documents. For data TeamCP does not hold, we will point you to the provider's procedure.

8. Your rights

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to access, correct or delete data, restrict or object to processing, withdraw consent, opt out of sale/sharing, or complain to a supervisory authority. Because TeamCP does not keep game data on its own servers, most requests are handled through device settings and the ad providers' procedures; requests about issue reports are handled by TeamCP directly. We will tell you which route to use.

9. Children and parents

CatWayOut is a puzzle game about guiding cats off the board in the direction they face. It contains ads and is not directed at children under 13. The app tells the ad services that it is not directed at children, and it has no age check or parental consent feature.

If you believe information from a child under 13 has been processed, please contact us and we will explain how to delete it.

10. Security and changes to this policy

Game data is kept in the app's private Android storage, which other apps cannot read. Ad and issue-report traffic uses encrypted connections (HTTPS).

If features, SDKs or processing change, we update this policy and its date first and announce important changes on this page. This document is available in eight languages; if you think the translations differ, please contact us. The Korean version prevails.

Additional notice under Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act (added November 23, 2026)

Under Article 30 of Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) and Article 31 of its Enforcement Decree, this notice explains your rights and how to exercise them, children under 14 and their legal guardians, the security measures we take, and our privacy officer. It applies together with the rest of this policy.

Your rights and how to exercise them

  • You may at any time ask TeamCP to give you access to, correct, delete, or suspend the processing of the personal information it processes about you, and you may withdraw your consent (PIPA Articles 35–37).
  • How to ask: email the app name and your request to the contact below (teamcp.channel@gmail.com). Because the app has no accounts, please include information that lets TeamCP find the record (for example, the approximate date or report number of a problem report). A legal guardian or a person you authorize may also make a request; in that case we may ask for proof of that relationship.
  • Response time: we will tell you the outcome within 10 days of receiving your request. If the law gives a reason to limit or refuse the request, or we cannot complete it within that time, we will tell you why and how to object.
  • Information stored only on your device (app records, settings, and so on) is not held by TeamCP, so you can delete it yourself with the app’s delete options, by clearing the app’s storage in Android settings, or by uninstalling the app.
  • For information processed by outside providers such as the ad services and Google, you can also contact each provider at the contact listed in the overseas transfer notice above.
  • Remedies in Korea: you can apply for dispute mediation or advice to the Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee (+82-1833-6972, www.kopico.go.kr), the Personal Information Infringement Report Center (118, privacy.kisa.or.kr), the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office (1301, www.spo.go.kr), or the Korean National Police Agency (182, ecrm.police.go.kr).

Children under 14 and legal guardians

  • Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act requires the consent of a legal guardian when the personal information of a child under 14 is processed on the basis of consent (Article 22-2).
  • This app does not ask for a date of birth or age, and it has no age check or way to confirm a guardian’s consent. Because it does not treat users differently by age, the processing described in this policy also applies to users under 14. The app tells the ad services, at app level, that it is “not directed to children”. This is not the result of checking any individual user’s age.
  • Personalized ads: on first launch the app asks whether to allow personalized ads and does not start the ad SDK until you choose. Users under 14 should not allow personalized ads and should choose the non-personalized option. If personalized ads were already allowed, you can change this in the app settings.
  • Users under 14 should not include personal information such as their name or contact details in problem reports or inquiries.
  • Guardians’ rights and how to exercise them: a legal guardian may ask for access to, correction, deletion, or suspension of processing of the child’s personal information, and may withdraw consent. The method and response time are the same as in “Your rights and how to exercise them” above. We ask only for the minimum information needed to confirm guardianship and delete it once confirmed.
  • If we learn that the personal information of a child under 14 has been processed without a legal guardian’s consent, we will promptly delete that information held by TeamCP.

Security measures for personal information

  • On-device storage: app records and settings are stored in the app-private storage that Android keeps separate for each app, and are not sent to servers operated by TeamCP except as described in this policy.
  • Encrypted transmission: information the app sends over the internet (ad requests, problem reports) is sent over encrypted connections (HTTPS/TLS).
  • Report server access limits: the problem-report server accepts only reports in a fixed format sent by registered apps, and stores app authentication values as hashes, not as the original values. Administrative access to the server and database is limited to TeamCP’s operator account. Reports do not automatically include the advertising ID, account, or location.
  • Data minimization: we do not collect sign-ups, passwords, names, or phone numbers, which keeps the personal information held by TeamCP to a minimum.
  • Retention and deletion: problem reports are deleted 90 days after receipt, or earlier if you ask us to delete them.
  • Inquiry emails are deleted once they are no longer needed after we have responded. Personal information is kept only as electronic files and is deleted when the retention period ends.
  • Security for information processed by outside providers such as the ad services and Google follows each provider’s policy.
